qe:
Directions: A $ B means A ≥ B; A © B means A > B; A @ B means A = B; A # B means A ≤ B; A % B means A < B.
Statements: M $ N ; N © T ; T @ U
Conclusions: I. M © T, II. N @ U
qh:
निर्देश: A $ B का अर्थ A ≥ B; A © B का अर्थ A > B; A @ B का अर्थ A = B; A # B का अर्थ A ≤ B; A % B का अर्थ A < B है।
कथन: M $ N ; N © T ; T @ U
निष्कर्ष: I. M © T, II. N @ U
e:
Method 1 (Coded Inequality Box Method Shortcut):
Step 1: Symbols decode karein:
- Statement: $M \ge N > T = U$.
Step 2: Conclusion I (M © T $\equiv M > T$):
- M se T tak: '≥' aur '>' me high priority '>' (©) ko milti hai $\implies M > T$ bilkul sahi hai (Follows).
Step 3: Conclusion II (N @ U $\equiv N = U$):
- N se U tak: $N > T = U \implies N > U$. Parantu conclusion me '=' diya hai (Does not follow).
Atah kewal I follow karta hai.
Correct option  Only I follows hai.

Method 2 (Direct Priority Inspection):
$M \ge N > T \implies M > T$ (I true). $N > U \ne N = U$ (II false). Kewal Conclusion I satya hai.
Sahi uttar 'Only I follows' hai.

Exam point: kathan-nishkarsh ka niyam - ise yaad rakhein; isi tarah ke prashn pariksha mein doharaaye jaate hain.

qe:
Directions (36–38): P ÷ Q means P = Q ; P + Q means P < Q ; P - Q means P > Q ; P × Q means P ≥ Q ; P $ Q means P ≤ Q.

Ex36. Statements: M + N ; R × N ; R $ U
Conclusions: I. M + R, II. U × N
qh:
निर्देश (36–38): P ÷ Q का अर्थ P = Q ; P + Q का अर्थ P < Q ; P - Q का अर्थ P > Q ; P × Q का अर्थ P ≥ Q ; P $ Q का अर्थ P ≤ Q है।

Ex36. कथन: M + N ; R × N ; R $ U
निष्कर्ष: I. M + R, II. U × N
e:
Method 1 (Coded Inequality Decoding & Priority Shortcut):
Step 1: Prateekon (Symbols) ko decode karein:
- `÷` $\implies =$
- `+` $\implies <$
- `-` $\implies >$
- `×` $\implies \ge$
- `$` $\implies $\le$$
Step 2: Statements decode karke ek chain banayein:
- $M < N$
- $R $\ge$ N \implies N $\le$ R$
- $R $\le$ U$
- Sanyukt chain: $M < N $\le$ R $\le$ U$.
Step 3: Conclusions evaluate karein:
- Conclusion I (`M + R` $\equiv M < R$): M se R tak '<' aur '≤' me high priority '<' ko milti hai $\implies M < R$ 100% satya hai (Follows).
- Conclusion II (`U × N` $\equiv U $\ge$ N$): U se N tak sabhi chinh '≥' parivar ke hain ($U $\ge$ R $\ge$ N \implies U $\ge$ N$) jo 100% satya hai (Follows).
Atah dono nishkarsh follow karte hain.
Correct option  Both I and II follow hai.

Method 2 (Direct Chain Inspection):
$M < N $\le$ R \implies M < R$ (I true). $N $\le$ R $\le$ U \implies U $\ge$ N$ (II true). Dono nishkarsh anivarya roop se satya hain.
Sahi uttar 'Both I and II follow' hai.

Exam point: kathan-nishkarsh ka niyam - ise yaad rakhein; isi tarah ke prashn pariksha mein doharaaye jaate hain.

qe:
Directions (36–38): P ÷ Q means P = Q ; P + Q means P < Q ; P - Q means P > Q ; P × Q means P ≥ Q ; P $ Q means P ≤ Q.

Ex37. Statements: P × Q ÷ R ; R × T
Conclusions: I. P - T, II. P ÷ T, III. Q × T
qh:
निर्देश (36–38): P ÷ Q का अर्थ P = Q ; P + Q का अर्थ P < Q ; P - Q का अर्थ P > Q ; P × Q का अर्थ P ≥ Q ; P $ Q का अर्थ P ≤ Q है।

Ex37. कथन: P × Q ÷ R ; R × T
निष्कर्ष: I. P - T, II. P ÷ T, III. Q × T
oe: Only either I or II and III follow
oh: Only either I or II and III follow
e:
Method 1 (Independent True + Either-Or Shortcut Trick):
Step 1: Statements decode karein:
- $P \ge Q = R$
- $R \ge T$
- Sanyukt chain: $P \ge Q = R \ge T$.
Step 2: P aur T ke beech relation dekhein:
- $P \ge T$ definite relation nikalta hai.
- $P \ge T$ do sambhavnaon me tootta hai: $P > T$ (`P - T`) ya $P = T$ (`P ÷ T`).
- Atah Conclusion I aur II ke beech 'Either I or II follows' banega.
Step 3: Q aur T ke beech relation dekhein:
- $Q = R \ge T \implies Q \ge T$ (`Q × T`) 100% nishchit satya hai (Conclusion III follows).
Step 4: Dono ko milane par: 'Only either I or II and III follow'.
Correct option  hai.

Method 2 (Sign Splitting Method):
Conclusion III direct satya hai. $P \ge T$ se '>' aur '=' ke liye Either-Or case banta hai. Sahi vikalp  hai.

Exam point: kathan-nishkarsh ka niyam - ise yaad rakhein; isi tarah ke prashn pariksha mein doharaaye jaate hain.

qe:
Directions (36–38): P ÷ Q means P = Q ; P + Q means P < Q ; P - Q means P > Q ; P × Q means P ≥ Q ; P $ Q means P ≤ Q.

Ex38. Statements: M - N ÷ T ; R × U ÷ N
Conclusions: I. M - R, II. M $ R, III. R - N, IV. R ÷ N
qh:
निर्देश (36–38): P ÷ Q का अर्थ P = Q ; P + Q का अर्थ P < Q ; P - Q का अर्थ P > Q ; P × Q का अर्थ P ≥ Q ; P $ Q का अर्थ P ≤ Q है।

Ex38. कथन: M - N ÷ T ; R × U ÷ N
निष्कर्ष: I. M - R, II. M $ R, III. R - N, IV. R ÷ N
oe: Only either I or II follows
Only either III or IV follows
oh: Only either I or II follows
Only either III or IV follows
e:
Method 1 (Dual Either-Or Identification Shortcut):
Step 1: Statements decode karein:
- $M > N = T$
- $R \ge U = N \implies R \ge N$.
Step 2: Conclusions evaluate karein:
- Case 1 (R aur N ke beech): $R \ge N$ definite hai. Yeh do bhagon me tootta hai: $R > N$ (`R - N`) ya $R = N$ (`R ÷ N`). Isse Conclusion III aur IV ke beech 'Either III or IV follows' banta hai.
- Case 2 (M aur R ke beech): $M > N \le R$. Yahan viprit chinh aane se condition block banta hai (no definite relation). Condition block me jab teeno chinh ($>$, $<$, $=$) shamil hon, toh Either-Or banta hai.
  - Conclusion I: $M > R$ (`M - R`)
  - Conclusion II: $M \le R$ (`M $ R`, arthath $<$ aur $=$)
  - Atah Conclusion I aur II ke beech bhi 'Either I or II follows' banega.
Step 3: Pura uttar 'Either I or II and either III or IV follow' hoga.
- Chuki yeh vikalp (A, B, C, D) me poora maujood nahi hai, atah (E) None of these sahi hai.
Correct option  None of these hai.

Method 2 (Exhaustive Pair Verification):
I aur II milkar 3-sign block condition ka Either-Or banate hain. III aur IV milkar '≥' ka Either-Or banate hain. Dono pairs valid hain, isliye 'None of these' sahi hai.

Exam point: kathan-nishkarsh ka niyam - ise yaad rakhein; isi tarah ke prashn pariksha mein doharaaye jaate hain.
